correctness.rationale: Disjoint interval sums for B_phi imply B_phi^n rows indexed by I_{n,j}=(phi^n(j−1),phi^n(j)] for j>=1 and root [0,phi^n(0)]. If some gap stays bounded, Holder and escape to infinity force each orbit’s j-coordinate to zero and preclude hypercyclicity. If all gaps grow, dense zero-sum finite-support vectors eventually map to 0 and the disjoint constant-block right inverses R_n have l^p norm→0 (p>1), yielding mixing. For explicit s_t=2^{floor(log2 log2(t+4))}, the map sends level J_t to J_{t+1} with scale ratio 1 or 2, so iterated gaps diverge; (B^n x)_1 uses disjoint blocks of size s_n/2<=log2(n+4)/2. Holder plus summation of disjoint input l^p masses yields the all-vector polylog visit bound, zero upper density, hence no upper frequent hypercyclic vectors. Exact small-level computations independently confirmed the interval iteration, not used as proof.
